problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=\frac{1}{4}t-{t}^{2},$ where $t>0$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=-7$ when $t=3,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=4{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+6t,$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=11$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,dt \\  & =\int (4{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+6t)dt \\  & ={t}^{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(1)=11.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =(1)^{4}+\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}+3(1)^{2}+C \\ 11 & =1+\frac{1}{3}+3+C \\ C & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)={t}^{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}+\frac{20}{3}.
$$
